analysis.title: From bad to worst: The 12 Charts You Need to See Before Monday's Open
key_insights: Tech has fallen well below its channel relative to the S&P 500 (Deutsche Bank).
Systematic positioning has turned modestly short but remains well above prior extremes, so CTAs and vol-control funds have room to keep selling.
S&P futures liquidity, measured by top-of-book depth, is at its lowest since April 2025 and mirrors other stressed episodes.
GS prime brokerage reports the heaviest week of single-stock shorting since June 2022, with short flow around 1.5% of gross market value.
Hedge Fund VIP drawdown is among the worst on record, putting performance fees at risk.
HF leverage decline from 12m highs matches some of the most extreme episodes since 2018 (JPM PI).
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3%, the 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 pts since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low (GS Prime).
Momentum exposure reversed from a record +70% in June to negative, the lowest since late 2022 (GS Prime).
S&P closed 4.10 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, the most oversold since August 25, 2015 (Bespoke).
Equity positioning is at levels historically associated with earnings contractions, so investors are already positioned for an earnings recession.
Median short interest is 3.1% and the 90th-percentile stock is at 8%, back toward 2008-2010 peaks. Prior similar periods saw violent squeezes (Goldman).
Deutsche Bank consolidated equity positioning is only at the 11th percentile since 2010, well above prior capitulation lows, so maximum fear may not have been reached.

sector_views.rationale: Tech trades well below its relative channel versus the S&P 500 amid the selloff.

earnings_insights: Equity positioning is consistent with earnings contractions, but the report notes it remains to be seen whether earnings will actually contract.
risk_factors: Further systematic selling given positioning is not yet at prior extremes.
Positioning is not at past capitulation lows, so downside may extend.
Actual earnings recession could validate bearish positioning.
Short squeeze risk given elevated short interest.

tension_points.bull_case: Many positioning readings are extreme (GFC-level short interest, record-low leverage, 4.10 sigma oversold), which historically precedes violent squeezes and rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: DB consolidated positioning is only at the 11th percentile and well above prior capitulation lows. Systematic funds still have room to sell and liquidity is thin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further decline in DB consolidated positioning toward prior capitulation lows would show the washout is not complete.

theme_stances.key_argument: Despite many extreme readings, consolidated positioning is not as bearish as prior capitulation lows, so maximum fear may not have been reached.
theme_stances.evidence: We might not have reached maximum fear yet.
